doc.title: Vince Giordano interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2007

chapter: Kenny Davern and the bass saxophone
title: A blindfold test with himself
summary: Monk plays a record with Keith Ingham and Joe Boughton; Vince fails to recognize his own bass saxophone.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Well I got to play with him a couple of times up at Hamilton College and I’m telling you it was a high point of my life just about. I brought in a little, this will be like a drop the needle test.
Oh wonderful, like a blindfold test, I’ve got my glasses on, good.
Yes. This is a sunglasses test. Let’s see if I got it up here.
You might want to be careful what you say about who this is. I like it.
Great stuff. Everybody’s doing the right stuff. Good bass sax guy
No, no. Maybe Dick Sudhalter on trumpet?
Is that me? I had no idea.

That’s interesting. See when I play things for people I don’t really — I usually play their own things so I could have given you a clue. But that’s with Keith Ingham and something on — I forget the record label — with Joe Boughton?

Oh really, okay. I don’t recognize my sound. I mean there was not enough in there, you know I was basically just keeping the time there. Wow okay. I survived my own blindfold test even though I don’t know it was me.
Well you did point out that it was a nice bass saxophone.
One of the those European guys or something.
